title: Dual-core with shared L2
decision: Implement two processor cores on a single chip, sharing an integrated L2 cache
alternatives_or_rejected: Possibility of a single core with larger L2 or separate L2 caches; the paper argues that shared L2 improves performance for multi-threaded workloads and reduces off‑chip traffic
rationale: Shared L2 provides lower latency for inter‑core data sharing and better utilization of cache resources
outcome: The POWER4 chip contains two cores, each with its own L1 I/D caches, and a shared 1.5 MB L2 cache, which became the foundation for the design

title: Clock frequency and pipeline depth
where_in_paper: Microarchitecture section, discussion of pipeline stages
decision: Use a relatively deep pipeline (seven stages for integer and more for floating‑point) to achieve a high clock frequency (target 1 GHz+)
alternatives_or_rejected: Shallower pipeline would reduce branch misprediction penalty but limit frequency; the paper notes that the aggressive frequency target was a primary design goal
rationale: Higher frequency was prioritized to meet performance objectives, despite increased branch misprediction penalties
outcome: The chip operated at 1.1–1.3 GHz in initial implementations, and the pipeline structure was detailed

title: RAS features: processor recovery
decision: Implement processor recovery mechanisms, including check‑stop and instruction retry, to handle transient errors
alternatives_or_rejected: The paper contrasts with simpler error‑detection schemes that only log errors without recovery; they chose to recover from many errors to improve availability
rationale: Maintaining system availability in enterprise servers was paramount, so error recovery was added despite area and complexity costs
outcome: POWER4 includes hardware support for instruction retry and machine check handling, improving reliability

title: Cache coherence protocol choice
where_in_paper: Microarchitecture section, cache and memory subsystem
decision: Adopt a distributed directory‑based cache coherence protocol
alternatives_or_rejected: Snoopy protocols were considered but were not scalable for the large system configurations (up to 32 processors) that POWER4 was designed to support
rationale: Directory‑based protocol scales better to larger SMP systems and reduces snoop bandwidth
outcome: The coherence protocol was implemented with a distributed directory, enabling glueless scaling to multiple chips

title: Power management: dynamic voltage and clocking
decision: Implement dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) support, as well as clock gating for idle units
alternatives_or_rejected: The paper mentions that without such measures, power consumption would exceed the thermal envelope; they chose to incorporate multiple power‑saving features
rationale: Meeting power and thermal limits while maintaining high performance required active power management
outcome: The chip features clock gating and frequency scaling, which allowed it to operate within its power budget
